title: Sysmon Event ID 10 (Process Access) — handle opened to LSASS by a credential-dumping tool
event_type: Sysmon operational log, Event ID 10 (Process Access), TargetImage lsass.exe

callouts.explanation: Confirms the accessed process is lsass.exe, the credential-material target described in section 4.1 — this field alone is not suspicious since many legitimate processes (AV/EDR agents, the OS itself) also open handles to LSASS.

The access-rights mask is the discriminating field: a broad mask like 0x1fffff (full access, typical of a full memory-dump tool) or a narrower memory-read mask such as 0x1010/0x1410 used by a targeted credential-dumping tool both indicate read access to LSASS memory, unlike harmless query-only access rights.

Identifies the requesting process; a signed, well-known dumping utility run from a non-standard user-writable path (Downloads, not an admin toolkit location) is itself part of the classification logic in section 2.2's tiering model.

The stack trace at the moment access was granted can show whether the request originated from a normal API call chain or from an unusual/unbacked module, a secondary signal analysts use to corroborate the GrantedAccess reading.
